options.raison: attach a file to an email

etapes.texte: Learn each word with its **partner**: meet a deadline
Read the words **around the blank**: contract, email
Be careful with words that __look alike__: attach, attend, attract

phrases.texte: Office and email vocabulary.
First, four email verbs. Attach means add a file: please attach the invoice.
phrases.dit: First, four email verbs. Attach, means add a file: please attach the invoice.

phrases.texte: Forward means send a message on to another person: I will forward it to Ms. Lee.
phrases.dit: Forward, means send a message on to another person: I will forward it to Miz Lee.

phrases.texte: Reply means answer. And submit means hand in: submit the form online.
phrases.dit: Reply, means answer. And submit, means hand in: submit the form online.

phrases.texte: Now, four nouns. A memo is a short note to the staff. A deadline is the final date.
A schedule is a plan of times. And supplies are paper, pens and other small things.
In the TOEIC, words go together. Learn them as pairs: meet a deadline.
Attend a meeting. Place an order.
One trap: two words with the same sound. Stationery, with an E, means paper, pens and envelopes.
phrases.dit: One trap: two words with the same sound. Stationery, with an E, means paper, pens and envelopes.

phrases.texte: Stationary, with an A, means not moving.
phrases.dit: Stationary, with an A, means not moving.

phrases.texte: Now, a TOEIC question. Please, blank, the signed contract to your email.
A: attend. B: attach. C: attract. D: attempt.
phrases.dit: Answer A. attend. Answer B. attach. Answer C. attract. Answer D. attempt.

phrases.texte: Which answer is correct?
The four words look alike. So read the words around the blank: contract, and email.
We attend a meeting, we attract customers, and attempt means try. They do not fit.
phrases.dit: We attend a meeting, we attract customers, and attempt, means try. They do not fit.

phrases.texte: B is correct: please attach the signed contract to your email.
Three steps. One: learn each word with its partner.
Two: read the words around the blank.
Three: be careful with words that look alike.
Now practise with the questions below.
phrases.dit: Now, practise with the questions below.
